requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`. I did not request implementation source. The three marked tests cover the subject's own obligations, and the cited requirements are context.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **Block mapping entries are `pair` items named by the written key.**
  - `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` outlines a YAML document with plain keys (`a`, `c`, `e`, `f`) and a quoted key (`"b"`).
  - It asserts the full `summary` list, including `pair[a]` and `pair["b"]`. The quoted key keeps its quotes, so the name is the key as written.
- **Flow mapping entries are `pair` items.** The same test has `c: {d: 1}` and asserts `pair["b"]/pair[c]/pair[d] 4-4`.
- **Block sequence entries are anonymous `item` items.** The same test asserts `.../pair[e]/item@ 6-6` for `- f: 1` and `.../pair[e]/item@ 7-7` for `- 2`. These show an anonymous item with a mapping child, and an anonymous item with a scalar.
- **Nested entries sit beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.** The asserted selectors in that test form a chain such as `pair["b"]/pair[e]/item@/pair[f]`. The `OutlineContent` selection tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` also select `pair[a]/pair[b]`.
- **The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends to include owned comments.**
  - The `summary` assertions include line ranges. The leading `# c` comment is included, so `pair[a] 1-2`. Nested spans are exact, for example `pair[e] 5-7`.
  - `yaml_selection_includes_comments_owned_by_the_entry` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` checks a trailing comment. The selected text of `pair[key]` is `key: value # trailing comment`, and the span is `0..len`.
  - The same test checks that `pair[d]` selects `# before next\nd: 2`, so the preceding comment is owned by the next entry. It also checks that `pair[a]` selects only `a:\n  b: 1`, so the span ends at the last non-comment token and excludes the next entry's comment.
- **Comment ownership follows `requirements.references.outline_comments`.** `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` checks a comment between sibling nested keys. `comment_owners_at_line(5)` returns exactly one owner, `pair[jobs]/pair[second]`. Ownership rules are cited rather than implemented here, so this is a supporting check.
- **Selector grammar, percent-encoding and duplicate-name suffixes follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.** This is a citation, so the subject adds no obligation of its own. The YAML tests still exercise the selector format in their assertions.

**Gaps considered**

I found none. Cases the text doesn't name are not gaps. These include several flow entries on one line, single-quoted keys and flow sequences.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
